chapter: Moten band, Kansas City and the evolution of jazz
title: Ralph Cooper at the Regal Theater and Reginald Forsythe's lesson in voicing
summary: Called from Minneapolis to the Regal Theater by Ralph Cooper, he shared a hotel room with Reginald Forsythe, who taught him how to space trombone parts. He recalls hearing Omar Simeon at the Metropolitan Theater.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So anyway, I stayed around there and then finally I went on back to Minneapolis. And I stayed around Minneapolis until finally I'd get a call, telegram to come to Chicago to play with Ralph Cooper at the Regal Theater.
This was Ralph Cooper who was in the movies?
Uh-huh. So I go over to play with Raoul because previously when I had been in Chicago before,

when I was with Bernie Young, I used to go often across the street to the Metropolitan Theater to hear Erskine Tate's band, to listen to Omar Simeon because there was another great clarinet and great saxophone player. Because I always went to hear the saxophone players, mostly.

But anyway, I went to Chicago to play with Ralph Cooper in the Regal Theater, and by him bringing me from Minneapolis there, they fired the whole band off the job. So Ralph Cooper and Reginald Forsythe who was writing for Earl Hines, we were all cooped up together at the Oakwood Boulevard there, that hotel was called, I think, the Ritz -- the Tremier (PHONETIC) Hotel it was called then, right next to the Grand Terrace on Oakwood Boulevard.

So all the folks bunked up there together in this room. And so I had some arrangements and I had never written for over one trombone at that time. So I just took an ad, Earl Hines had two trombones. So I added another trombone part to my (SOPRANO SAX) (UNINTELLIGIBLE), took him over for Earl to play and they sounded terrible with this other added trombone part and I couldn't figure it out. So Reginald Forsythe, he showed me how to VOICE the trombones so they wouldn't -- I just added the part, and that's how I first learned how to space the brass out, from him.
